seo.title: Elasticsearch client for {devices}
seo.description: Send Query DSL from a console, browse Elasticsearch indices as tables, filter, sort and edit documents by _id, signed in with a password or API key.

header.title: Elasticsearch client
header.lead: Run Query DSL requests from a console, browse index documents in a grid and edit them by their IDs.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter the REST host and port, then choose an Auth Method: Username & Password, API Key or None. API keys use the encoded value from Elasticsearch, and each connection reaches one cluster.

New connections start with SSL Disabled, which is plain HTTP; every other mode uses HTTPS. Preferred and Required (skip verify) accept a self-signed certificate, and Verify CA and Verify Identity check it. Elasticsearch 8.x turns security and TLS on by default, so an 8.x cluster usually needs HTTPS and credentials.

bands.title: Indices and the Query DSL console
text: Write a method, path and optional JSON body, such as GET /orders/_search. Search hits and array responses display as rows, other responses as formatted JSON, and the _sql endpoint is not available.

The sidebar lists indices as tables and hides names that begin with a dot. Columns come from the mapping: object fields flatten to dotted paths such as address.city, a nested field gets one JSON column for its array plus a column per leaf, and every document carries _id, _index and _score.

Column filters become term, range, wildcard, terms and exists queries, and the Raw SQL filter row takes Lucene syntax, such as name:Widget. Edits go out as REST calls by _id; change a nested array through its JSON column.
notes: TablePro also connects to <search>Typesense and Weaviate</search>, the other search engines.

bands.title: Mappings
text: Mappings are read-only. Truncate is not offered, because the nearest thing Elasticsearch has, _delete_by_query, runs asynchronously and reports conflicts per document; send it from the console. Deleting an index from the sidebar sends the DELETE request its confirmation shows.

moveData: Export reads a whole index with a point-in-time and search_after, so it is not capped at the result window, and writes {exportFormats}.

faq.question: Can I page past the result window?
faq.answer: Yes. Paging past Elasticsearch’s default window switches to search_after over a point-in-time. The switch happens at the default, so an index with a lowered max_result_window errors first; raise the setting back to the default.

faq.question: Why does sorting by _id leave the rows in the same order?
faq.answer: Elasticsearch cannot sort on _id, or on a text field with no .keyword subfield, so TablePro drops that column from the sort. Add a keyword subfield to the mapping, or sort on a keyword field.
